prompt.text:
Continue from the still. the Explorer in an ivory industrial helmet with an opaque black full-face visor and cyan side-light rings, orange technical coveralls, chest instrument and grey boots is inside a cooling loaf as steam drifts and the crumb firms, soft warm light. Photoreal cinematic scientific visualization, warm polished home realism, ivory-and-orange equipment palette, cyan accent light. Low motion.

At the opening of the shot, Steam thins slowly. Ambient (slow, subtle): the crumb settles and light softens.

Then, The single Explorer stays planted at the left edge, feet still, head raised toward camera, and says over helmet radio in a calm adult male English voice: "It smells finished. How can you be sure?" His mouth returns to rest.

Then, The Explorer holds still, head tilted, while Control answers in a calm adult English voice: "Colour, a hollow sound, and a set crumb tell your baker it is done. Cooling finishes the work; slice too early and the soft middle turns gummy. Patience is an ingredient here." The Explorer stays in place, mouth closed.

Finally, The camera begins a slow dolly out. The camera ends on the firming crumb and thinning steam. Acoustic environment: a tap on crust and quiet cooling; clear close dialogue front and center. The Explorer stays in frame, mouth closed.

Reference lock: continue directly from the supplied still/reference image; it is the authoritative first frame and starting composition. Preserve the exact character identities, character count, wardrobes, set layout, lighting, and every visible prop's physical size, shape, placement, and attachment. Animate only the character actions explicitly requested in the scene direction. Keep all unattended characters, props, and background elements stationary within the scene. Follow the camera movement explicitly requested in the scene direction; if none is requested, keep the camera locked to the reference framing. Directed camera motion may change framing, perspective, screen positions, apparent size, and visibility without physically moving or changing the scene's objects. Do not introduce, duplicate, physically remove, relocate, reshape, or float any character or prop.
